title: Client-side inference simulator — quick sandbox
content:
One-line idea:
Build a lightweight client-side simulator that lets engineers and product folks preview token counts, estimated cost, and latency distribution for common prompt patterns before sending to Redwood. Aim: reduce surprise bill + speed up prompt iteration, especially for PLG signups and embedded SDKs.

Why useful / problem statement:
- Teams frequently tweak prompts and iterate blindly — only learn cost after calls.
- Simple heuristics (tokenizer counts) are helpful but insufficient: different model variants, context-window effects, streaming vs non-streaming, prefix caching change cost/latency.
- For onboarding and SDKs, a local preview reduces churn and lowers support volume.

MVP (user-facing):
- UI: small explorer pane in SDK/devtools or CLI. Paste prompt + select model variant + session options (streaming, max_tokens, stop) -> outputs: token breakdown (prompt/system/user), estimated token price (hosted price table), rough latency bucket (p50/p95) and confidence level.
- Core simulation: tokenizer + simple autoregressive token time model (token ms per model on given hw), naive KV-cache modeling for repeated prefixes, streaming vs chunked encoding.
- Exportable estimation: copyable JSON with billing estimate, tokens, and confidence notes.

MVP non-user pieces (infra/devx):
- Maintain small public price/latency profile JSON for each Redwood model variant (hosted, dedicated shapes, private defaults).
- Lightweight JS/TS library for tokenizer + estimator; no network calls required.

User stories:
- As an engineer, I want to paste a prompt and see estimated cost so I can choose cheaper templates for large-scale usage.
- As a PM evaluating plans, I want to simulate high-volume bursts to see monthly spend projection.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to capture an estimate to put in a customer proposal.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Local estimator returns tokens and cost estimate with +/- 20% accuracy vs hosted for typical English prompts (short-medium length).
- Web/CLI explorer shows p50/p95 latency heuristics for selected model variants.
- Library packaged as npm and PyPI (small optional dependency on tokenizer wasm or micropack).

API sketch (devx lib):
- estimate(prompt, modelVariant, {streaming: bool, history: [string], maxTokens: int}) -> {tokens: {prompt: int, completionCap: int}, costUsd: number, latencyMs: {p50: number, p95: number}, confidence: "low|medium|high", notes: [string]}

Open questions / risks:
- How to model private/dedicated latency without exposing internal perf numbers? Option: surface only relative tiers (fast/medium/slow) for private.
- Tokenizer binary size vs shipping in-browser — use wasm tokenizer, lazy-load.
- Pricing: hosted rates change; need a pinned version of price table per SDK release or call home to update. For privacy-minded users need offline price file.
- Accuracy for non-English / multimodal inputs. Start English-only, textual.

Data needs / profile table idea:
- model_variant, hw_class (A100/RTX/etc), tokens_per_ms_mean, tokens_per_ms_p95, price_per_1k_tokens_usd, streaming_penalty_factor

Metrics to track (if we do in-console with opt-in):
- Estimation used -> actual cost deviation distribution
- Click-through: estimate -> send request conversion rate (reduction suggests value)

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal devx-only tool + library (1 sprint).
- Phase 1: ship SDK integration + small devtools pane in console for self-serve users (opt-in) (2 sprints).
- Phase 2: add batch/burst projection for enterprise quoting + export CSV (follow-up).

Notes to self / todo:
- Prototype tokenizer wasm wrapper (look at tiktoken-wasm forks).
- Get sample perf table from infra (request A: perf summary per model on hosted); if blocked, use historical benchmarks we published.
- Quick UX: minimal explorer in draft console -> patterns: single prompt, prompt+history, batch CSV input.
- Keep language simple in UI: show a range and confidence; avoid hard guarantees.

Random brainstorm ideas (future):
- Suggest cheaper paraphrases automatically (small local paraphraser) to cut token count by X% with low quality hit.
- “What-if” slider to test different temperature/top_p/weirdness impact on token length distribution.
- Embed cost annotations inline in prompt editor (hover token shows incremental price).

Links / references:
- proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-playground (WIP)
- prior notes: /confluence/client-sim-playground

-- end scratchpad --
